title: POC Weekly: Onboarding Pulse, Access Handoff & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on access handoff, staging environment readiness, and first-pass inference benchmarks. Agreed next steps: SE to run focused latency tests with prefix caching toggled, AE to share cost/quantization doc, customer to provision cross-account role and test buzzer endpoint. Discussed a spurious token inflation observed in early runs and an SSO/KMS clarification. Decided to schedule a short private-deploy readiness call next week if staging passes internal checks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-11
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 34 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood CSM), Elena Moore (Novus Platform Eng), Dan Rios (Novus DevOps), Priya Shah (Novus ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Product), Speaker 6

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Quick check on onboarding progress, keys/roles, and a weird token inflation observed in early bench runs. Agreed actions and owners.

Transcript:
00:00 Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. we can do a quick round — status, blockers, then bench recap. Sofia, want to kick off?
00:10 Sofia Ramos: yeah short one — Elena and team reported creds were partially there last night, looks like there was a missing trust relationship for the cross-account role, elena, is that right?
00:20 Elena Moore: yep that's correct, we added the role but missed the principal that Redwood needs. fixed it at about 10pm PST but didn't test again. so this morning we retested and had a 403 on the gateway call.
00:33 Dan Rios: and the egress rules in our staging VPC blocked the initial handshake, we patched that in the firewall rules at 02:00 and then saw traffic but some requests timed out.
00:45 Marcus Patel: timing out — was that at the TCP layer or the TLS handshake? sometimes timeouts look like TLS because SNI mismatch. any logs?
00:52 Dan Rios: a mixture, but mostly 504 gateway timeouts. the flask sidecar threw a read timeout before the response from the Redwood endpoint.
01:02 Priya Shah: from the ML side we ran the first 100 sample passes overnight with the redwood-hosted model. we observed two odd things: one, the avg latency was close to your profile but p99 spiked to 1.2s on a handful of prompts; two, token counts were about 18% higher than expected when prefix caching was enabled.
01:20 Avery Chen: 18% token inflation, that's notable. can you paste an example? is it coming from whitespace normalization or maybe streaming chunk duplicates?
01:28 Priya Shah: i'll share snippets in the spreadsheet, but one hypothesis is that the app prepends a JSON metadata blob per request which isn't being deduped by your prefix cache. so the cache thinks the prefix is unique every time.
01:42 Marcus Patel: ah that makes sense — prefix cache keys are exact-string sensitive. if you're writing metadata with timestamps that's a new prefix every call. we have two mitigation paths: strip the metadata before sending for inference, or normalize the metadata to a stable token.
01:56 Elena Moore: how invasive is that change in our infra? usually the metadata is added in the app layer just before request, it's easy to move upstream.
02:03 Tom Alvarez: product question — if we normalize, do we risk losing telemetry detail? we rely on request-level IDs for tracing.
02:11 Marcus Patel: you can keep telemetry locally — send an opaque key to Redwood that maps back in your logs. that keeps the cache working. we've done that pattern with other customers.
02:22 Priya Shah: ok i'll try mapping IDs rather than full metadata. we'll run another 10-sample test after Dan confirms the egress patch.
02:31 Avery Chen: to be clear on access — elena and dan, once the role is configured, can you confirm the ARN and we'll try a short handshake?
02:39 Elena Moore: yes i'll paste the ARN in the slack channel after the call.
02:43 Dan Rios: i'll retest egress rules and update the ticket, i saw a couple of dropped packets that looked like our proxy was rewriting the host header.
02:52 Marcus Patel: proxy host header rewrites can break TLS SNI. recommend bypassing for the handshake or adding exception.
03:00 Dan Rios: noted, will do.
03:05 Avery Chen: ok bench results — priya, can you summarize what you ran and the numbers you saw?
03:12 Priya Shah: we ran 100 prompts from our internal set: mix of short and medium instructions. avg latency ~160ms, p95 ~400ms, p99 spikes to 1.2s but only on 6 calls. token delta when prefix caching on vs off was +18% tokens on average; cost estimate bumped accordingly.
03:30 Marcus Patel: do you have the exact prompt that produced the spike? any pattern on sequence length or model temperature?
03:36 Priya Shah: two of them were long-ish user prompts with lots of code blocks; sequence length went up to 1.2k tokens. temp was default.
03:44 Marcus Patel: long sequences can trigger different kernel paths and also increase KV cache pressure which can yield p99 spikes if eviction occurs. also if batching changed mid-run you might see inconsistent latencies.
03:55 Elena Moore: what's batching changing mid-run mean? our client uses a short timeout to flush — could that be the cause?
04:02 Marcus Patel: yeah, if your client-side batcher sometimes flushes at 5ms and sometimes at 50ms, the server's runtime may flip between batched and singleton; that can affect p99. we can instrument traces to confirm.
04:15 Priya Shah: we don't currently emit batch size metrics to our app logs, we can add that quickly.
04:20 Avery Chen: this is sounding actionable: SE to run sweep for prefix cache on/off and for controlled batch sizes. Marcus, can you do that?
04:27 Marcus Patel: yep i'll run microbenchmarks — I'll do batch size 1/4/8 and with cache enabled/disabled against the same prompt set. will attach CSV.
04:35 Tom Alvarez: any security questions — we need SOC 2 language and KMS flow for our security team, they asked about who holds keys.
04:44 Avery Chen: for hosted POC the customer retains encryption keys in their KMS and we use a bring-your-own-key flow for payload encryption at rest. we can send the KMS integration checklist.
04:55 Elena Moore: is there any audit trail for token-level access? our compliance team wants per-request logs for 90 days.
05:03 Sofia Ramos: we provide audit logs and per-request metadata export for enterprise, retention is configurable as an add-on. i'll send the retention tiers.
05:11 Dan Rios: also our infra team wants to validate SAML SSO via our Okta — any blockers?
05:17 Avery Chen: SAML is supported, you'll need to create an app in Okta and we'll exchange metadata. we have a short-runbook for it.
05:25 Priya Shah: small note — when we enabled streaming w/ the SDK we saw duplicate tokens in the stream and the client occasionally concatenated chunks incorrectly which inflated token count; could be our client-side assembly bug.
05:36 Marcus Patel: that's classic if you double-apply a normalization step on streaming deltas. we'll share a debug snippet.
05:42 Elena Moore: ok so two possible sources for token inflation: app metadata + client streaming assembly. we'll test both.
05:50 Avery Chen: summary of next steps — Marcus does controlled bench, Avery shares docs/spreadsheet, Novus configures role and egress, Priya and Dan run the 10-sample smoke. Sofia will coordinate the private-deploy readiness calendar.
06:05 Tom Alvarez: timeline — if we can run smoke tests by Thursday (2026-05-13) we could do private-deploy readiness meeting on Monday (2026-05-18). is that realistic?
06:14 Elena Moore: yes Thursday sounds doable for the smoke tests.
06:18 Dan Rios: will aim for Thursday EOD.
06:21 Priya Shah: will run the 10-sample and the 100-sample spike reproducer and share token diffs.
06:28 Avery Chen: great. anything else?
06:31 Speaker 6: quick question — are there limits on prefix cache size that we should be aware of?
06:37 Marcus Patel: we size cache per-pod and it's configurable, default is 512MB but we can bump it for your Dedicated pool if needed in pilot.
06:46 Elena Moore: might need bump for long sequences, noted.
06:50 Avery Chen: ok final recap: action items will be posted in the CRM with owners, AE to send benchmark sheet and quant guidance, SE to share raw latency CSV and batch-size sweep, customer to confirm role ARN and complete smoke tests, CSM to schedule readiness call.
07:04 Sofia Ramos: i'll set the calendar and invite required security contacts for the KMS conversation.
07:10 Avery Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in slack and post artifacts in the shared drive. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: names and acronyms may be slightly off, some timestamps approximate.
